saints.name: St. John of God
saints.title: Religious, Founder of the Brothers Hospitallers
saints.shortBlurb: A soldier and shepherd whose sudden conversion led him to spend his life nursing the sick and the poor of Granada…
biography: Born João Duarte Cidade at Montemor-o-Novo in Portugal on 8 March 1495, John was lost to his family as a child and grew up a shepherd near Oropesa in Spain, then a soldier under its Count, fighting the French at Fontarabia and the Turks.

After years of wandering and a season in Ceuta nursing an exiled family, he settled at Granada as a seller of books. On 20 January 1537 a sermon of St. John of Ávila pierced him; his public penance was so violent he was shut in the mad ward of the Royal Hospital, where the preacher bade him serve others rather than scourge himself.

He rented a house for the sick poor of Granada, begging for them in the streets by night and nursing them by day. Companions joined him, and from them grew the Brothers Hospitallers, approved by the Holy See in 1572.

He died at Granada on 8 March 1550, his fifty-fifth birthday, of pneumonia caught after plunging into a river to save a drowning youth. Canonized by Pope Alexander VIII in 1690, he is patron of hospitals, the sick, and nurses for this work of mercy, and of booksellers from his earlier trade.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Brothers Hospitallers and his heroic care of the sick.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 8 March
